summary.headline: NDR Auto Q1 FY27 revenue INR221.45 crore with EBITDA margin 11.88% and PAT INR16.40 crore; management guides 11-12% margin ahead.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR221.45 crore with EBITDA of INR26.44 crore (11.88% margin) and PAT of INR16.40 crore, despite sector commodity and supply-chain pressure. The company commenced NDR Hayashi sunshade operations in Bangalore in June 2026 and inaugurated the NDR Auto South seat-trim plant at Anantapur, with SOP guided for Q2 FY27. Management reiterated an INR3,000 crore revenue endeavour by 2030 (INR2,000 crore organic plus INR1,000 crore inorganic) and guided Bharat Seats to about INR3,500 crore by 2030. Order book is about INR650 crore, unchanged from last quarter per the call, and management said it is bidding for much more business.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth of 19.5% as cited by analyst (YoY); not restated by management

Consolidated JV loss for the quarter

financial_highlights.change: Similar to last quarter per analyst

segments.name: NDR Auto Components (seat frames, seat covers, non-seat)
segments.commentary: Seat frames and covers make up most of the order book; new ambient lighting orders for Maruti Suzuki are a smaller part, with start in 2028. Management says non-seat margins will be similar to seating, though new-product ROCEs will be slightly lower.

segments.name: Bharat Seats (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 35% in Q1 FY27, which management said exceeded expectations; revenue target raised to about INR3,500 crore by 2030 from INR3,000-3,500 crore earlier. Premiumisation (ventilated/AC seats) flows to Bharat Seats as final assembler.

segments.name: NDR Auto South (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Anantapur seat-trim and frame plant inaugurated; production starts in Q2 FY27 with revenue potential of INR70-80 crore at full run-rate, subject to model performance. Debt funding converted into equity.

segments.name: NDR Hayashi (JV)
segments.commentary: Sunshade production began in Bangalore in June 2026; JV is loss-making and expected to break even at about INR100-150 crore revenue. Original 5-6 year potential was INR200-300 crore.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected at about 11% to 12%, with commodities indexed to pass-through costs.
ROCE and margins expected to remain at similar levels as the business expands.
Capex of about INR40-50 crore annually for the next couple of years; INR150 crore combined capex across plants with asset turnover of about 4x.
INR3,000 crore revenue by 2030 remains an endeavour: about INR2,000 crore organic and INR1,000 crore inorganic (still being worked on).
Management expects a slight uptick in revenue growth as the South plant, SBR, NDR Safety and Latch projects start (early next year).
Hayashi JV losses to continue for some quarters until break-even; Aurangabad plant to be set up only after Toyota business is secured, with Toyota plant now seen starting calendar 2029.
capex_capacity: NDR Hayashi sunshade plant at Bangalore commenced operations in June 2026.
NDR Auto South plant at Anantapur inaugurated; SOP from Q2 FY27, with about INR8 crore extra spend mentioned on the South unit.
Upcoming plants: seat insert, seat latch, and seatbelt reminder system; NDR Safety, SBR and Latch projects starting early next year.
Two empty lands held; new plant to be announced only after acquiring business viable for it. Aurangabad land acquired, plant pending Toyota business.
Management said it has over one million seats made, supporting scale-based cost advantage.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR650 crore; management says it is bidding for much more business and will confirm quarterly.
Brezza: company supplies 100% of the model, same as outgoing model.
No customer pressure to cut selling prices; cost increases offset by operational efficiencies.
Diversification: Toyota and Kia bids in progress; other OEMs being worked with; Maruti remains core client.
Growth in Q1 seen as market-driven; Bharat Seats growth attributed to a strong market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sequentially and YoY, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited marketing spend for new customers and R&D on prototypes; costs will continue as the company grows aggressively, and it has hired people, so the current run-rate is the new normal.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hayashi JV losses shrink?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses will continue for some quarters until sales reach break-even, estimated at INR100-150 crore revenue; the full team and overhead are already in place while the plant is still small.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hayashi and Anantapur contribute by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunshade business has started; ambient lighting contributes from 2028; South plant revenue to start in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise the 2030 target upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bharat Seats should be about INR3,500 crore by 2030; the group INR3,000 crore target remains an endeavour.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose an EBITDA margin target for 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a top-line target and declined to share an EBITDA margin range beyond the 11-12% near-term view.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aurangabad plant timing linked to Toyota?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant set-up depends on winning Toyota business; management agreed Toyota's plant is now seen starting calendar 2029, so the timeline is pushed.

risks_watch: Hayashi JV losses continue until break-even at INR100-150 crore revenue; Toyota project delay pushes timeline.
Rising other expenses (marketing, R&D, hiring) could pressure margins if revenue growth lags.
Concentration on Maruti Suzuki; diversification to Toyota and Kia not yet won.
Order book flat at about INR650 crore QoQ; watch confirmations of new business.
Commodity cost pass-through via indexation; watch for pressure on the 11-12% margin band.
NDR South ramp-up and contribution not quantified by management; to be shared with results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and margins, with optimism on growth and Bharat Seats; cautious and evasive on specifics such as order-book breakdown, EBITDA margin guidance beyond 11-12%, Hayashi break-even timing, and the product mix of trims to frames.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins remained healthy at 11.88%, despite the environmental and supply chain challenges the sector has been faced with.
We are not facing any pressure from customers to reduce selling price. We have actually been able to set off our cost increases with operational efficiencies.
So, we will continue to have losses for some quarters until we touch a break-even point for sales.
